The D1 bars fell from 104.04 (30 Oct high) to 84.237[Capital Chronicle](https://x.com/Capitalnicle)[@Capitalnicle](https://x.com/Capitalnicle)[16s](https://x.com/Capitalnicle/status/2120031760952246659)(9 Nov low), each bounce failed (91.449 on 6 Nov and 90.464 on 9 Nov were sold), and 9 Nov opened at 89.50 and closed at 85.547, below the 5 Nov low of 86.02, on US-Iran deal hopes and the Hormuz framework report. WTI is a net receiver in the connectedness row and its 20-day[Capital Chronicle](https://x.com/Capitalnicle)[@Capitalnicle](https://x.com/Capitalnicle)[15s](https://x.com/Capitalnicle/status/2120031763611468021)correlation with the S&P 500 is -0.55.[Capital Chronicle](https://x.com/Capitalnicle)[@Capitalnicle](https://x.com/Capitalnicle)[14s](https://x.com/Capitalnicle/status/2120031766413258950)• What is priced: drift -1.00 ATR from the 6 Nov close of 89.483 to the 85.584 capture; 5-day -2.62 ATR (-10.7%); 10-day -15.4%; 20-day mean 96.72 (z -2.09), 50-day 94.36 (z -1.87), 200-day 88.74; 20-day range 84.24-104.04; prior pricing AMBIGUOUS.[Capital Chronicle](https://x.com/Capitalnicle)[@Capitalnicle](https://x.com/Capitalnicle)[15s](https://x.com/Capitalnicle/status/2120031769051500706)• Positioning: speculators net long 80,289, only 4.2% of 1,908,732 open interest (COT as of 3 Nov, before the fall from 95.8 to 84.2), modest fuel below 84.2; shorts cover above 88.2. • Today's driver: clear, the Iran premium, and the D1 bars agree.[Capital Chronicle](https://x.com/Capitalnicle)[@Capitalnicle](https://x.com/Capitalnicle)[14s](https://x.com/Capitalnicle/status/2120031771526058092)• Reaction so far: accepted; the 9 Nov close of 85.547 sits near the 84.237 low and below 86.02, and Asia steadies near 85.6. • Why this zone: pullback zone 86.30-86.70 at the broken shelf of the 5 Nov D1 low 86.02 (bar open 2026-11-05T00:00Z) and the 4 Nov low 86.59; breakout[Capital Chronicle](https://x.com/Capitalnicle)[@Capitalnicle](https://x.com/Capitalnicle)[14s](https://x.com/Capitalnicle/status/2120031773983920460)zone 83.95-84.10 below the nearest support, the 9 Nov D1 low of 84.237 (bar open 2026-11-09T00:00Z); both known 2026-11-10T00:24:18.044Z.[Capital Chronicle](https://x.com/Capitalnicle)[@Capitalnicle](https://x.com/Capitalnicle)[13s](https://x.com/Capitalnicle/status/2120031776479563801)• What confirms it: (1) the repeated bounce failures at 91.449 and 90.464 and the close below 86.02 in the D1 bars; (2) the -0.55 the S&P 500 correlation in the WTI quant card, consistent with a supply rather than a demand move.[Capital Chronicle](https://x.com/Capitalnicle)[@Capitalnicle](https://x.com/Capitalnicle)[12s](https://x.com/Capitalnicle/status/2120031779205922819)• Alternative mechanism: stalled talks or Hormuz incidents restore the supply premium; which may be an escalation headline. • Invalidation: a completed H1 close above 88.35, or official confirmation of strikes that disrupt supply or a Hormuz closure.[Capital Chronicle](https://x.com/Capitalnicle)[@Capitalnicle](https://x.com/Capitalnicle)[12s](https://x.com/Capitalnicle/status/2120031781609205839)Analysis, not financial advice.
